patient.name: Nicole Farrow
patient.chiefComplaint: Found by roommate after intentional overdose, empty pill bottle nearby

history.hpi: Roommate returned home to find the patient drowsy and confused on the couch, with an empty amitriptyline bottle on the coffee table that had roughly 30 pills two days ago. Roommate reports patient sent a concerning text message about an hour before being found and estimates she took the pills sometime in the last hour.
medications: Amitriptyline 50 mg PO nightly (prescribed for depression/insomnia)
history.events: Roommate found an empty pill bottle and a concerning text message; called 911 immediately

scene.dispatch: 34-year-old female, altered mental status, possible overdose, residence
scene.location: Shared apartment, living room, patient on the couch
scene.safety: Empty pill bottle secured by roommate; no weapons or other hazards noted, but patient safety/self-harm risk present
scene.bystanders: Roommate present, found the empty bottle and a concerning text, provided timeline
visualCues: Empty amitriptyline bottle on the coffee table
Patient drowsy, slumped on the couch
Concerning text message shown on roommate's phone

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 34-year-old female with an intentional amitriptyline overdose approximately one hour ago, now drowsy, tachycardic, and hypotensive.

otherFindings: Empty amitriptyline bottle confirmed by roommate

expectedActions.shortAction: Ensure scene and patient safety given the intentional, self-harm nature of the ingestion
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Scene/environmental safety for patient and clinician
expectedActions.rationale: Intentional overdoses carry ongoing self-harm risk and require continued vigilance during care and transport.

expectedActions.shortAction: Continuously monitor ECG with specific attention to QRS duration
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Monitor EKG with special attention to rate, rhythm, QRS and QT duration
expectedActions.rationale: QRS widening is the key marker of TCA cardiotoxicity and guides the decision to give sodium bicarbonate.

expectedActions.shortAction: Sodium bicarbonate 65 mEq IV (65 kg × 1 mEq/kg), repeat as needed to narrow QRS and improve BP
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Tricyclic Antidepressant (TCA)/Sodium Channel Blocker Overdose — If widened QRS (100 msec or greater), consider sodium bicarbonate 1–2 mEq/kg IV, this can be repeated as needed to narrow QRS and improve blood pressure
expectedActions.rationale: Sodium bicarbonate is the definitive prehospital treatment for TCA-induced sodium channel blockade and QRS widening.

transitions.condition: Crew places the patient on a cardiac monitor with attention to QRS duration, establishes IV access, and ensures scene/patient safety given the intentional nature of the ingestion.

transitions.if: Sodium bicarbonate withheld despite widened QRS
transitions.condition: Despite the identified QRS widening, the crew does not administer sodium bicarbonate, and the cardiotoxicity progresses.

phases.name: Monitor placed, widened QRS identified
phases.description: Crew places the patient on a cardiac monitor with close attention to QRS duration given the known TCA ingestion, identifying a widened QRS consistent with sodium channel blockade, and establishes IV access.
phases.triggerCondition: The crew places the patient on a monitor with specific attention to QRS duration and identifies a widened QRS (112 msec) consistent with TCA sodium channel blockade; IV access is established.

expectedActions.shortAction: Repeat vital signs and ECG frequently; monitor closely for rapid deterioration
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Repeat vital signs often. Frequent reassessment is essential as patient deterioration can be rapid and catastrophic
expectedActions.rationale: TCA toxicity can deteriorate suddenly even after initial improvement.

transitions.condition: Given the widened QRS of 112 msec, the crew administers IV sodium bicarbonate, repeating as needed to narrow the QRS and improve blood pressure.

phases.name: Sodium bicarbonate given, QRS narrows
phases.description: Sodium bicarbonate is administered for the widened QRS, and the crew reassesses to confirm the QRS is narrowing along with improving blood pressure, repeating the dose as needed.
phases.triggerCondition: IV sodium bicarbonate is given for the QRS widening; the crew monitors for QRS narrowing and blood pressure improvement, repeating the dose as needed.

otherFindings: Repeat 12-lead shows QRS narrowing to 96 msec

phases.name: QRS narrowed, stable for transport
phases.description: The patient remains stable with a narrowed QRS and improving vital signs. The crew maintains continuous cardiac monitoring, patient safety precautions, and transports for definitive toxicology and psychiatric care.
phases.triggerCondition: After sodium bicarbonate and continued monitoring, the QRS remains narrowed and vitals are stable; crew transports with continued cardiac monitoring and safety precautions.

phases.name: Sodium bicarbonate withheld despite widened QRS
phases.description: Sodium bicarbonate is not given despite the identified QRS widening. The cardiotoxicity progresses, with further QRS widening, worsening hypotension, and new seizure activity.
phases.triggerCondition: Without sodium bicarbonate, the sodium channel blockade worsens: QRS continues to widen, blood pressure drops further, and the patient develops a seizure.

otherFindings: Repeat 12-lead shows QRS widened to 148 msec

expectedActions.shortAction: Give rescue sodium bicarbonate 65-130 mEq IV (65 kg × 1-2 mEq/kg) now for progressive QRS widening
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If widened QRS (100 msec or greater), consider sodium bicarbonate 1–2 mEq/kg IV, this can be repeated as needed to narrow QRS and improve blood pressure
expectedActions.rationale: Rescue bicarbonate is still indicated once the deterioration is recognized, though earlier administration would have prevented this progression.

expectedActions.shortAction: Treat the seizure per the Seizures Guideline if it recurs or persists
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: For seizure, treat per Seizures Guideline
expectedActions.rationale: TCA-induced seizures are treated per standard seizure management alongside bicarbonate therapy.
